query: We are a US company running an AI model on servers in the United States. Our customers are EU businesses that use the outputs of the system inside the Union. Does the EU AI Act apply to us even though we are not established in the EU?
A university research lab is developing a new machine learning system exclusively for scientific research. The system is not placed on the market or put into service. Is it covered by the AI Act?
We publish our recommendation engine under a free and open-source licence. Are we exempt from the AI Act, and are there cases where the exemption does not apply?
We build an AI tool and sell it under our own brand, while our customer companies use it internally. Who counts as provider and who as deployer under the AI Act?
How does the AI Act define a deep fake, and what kind of content falls under this definition?
What does 'intended purpose' mean under the AI Act, and where does it come from, for example sales brochures or instructions for use?

A loan-marketing app targets people in serious financial difficulty, using an AI that detects their economic vulnerability to push them into expensive credit products they would not otherwise choose. Is this permitted?

Police want to use real-time facial recognition in a train station to locate a missing child. Under what conditions can such a real-time remote biometric identification system be used, and what safeguards are required?

In an urgent situation a law enforcement authority started using real-time remote biometric identification in a public square before getting any authorisation. Is that allowed, and what must happen afterwards?
What is the maximum administrative fine for placing on the market or using an AI system that falls under the prohibited practices?
A small start-up (SME) breached its obligations as a deployer of a high-risk AI system. What is the maximum fine, and how does the SME status change the calculation?

Our AI tool for a lender is advertised as high-impact but it only classifies incoming documents and also builds personality profiles of applicants to support decisions about essential services. Can we claim the Article 6(3) derogation and avoid high-risk classification?
An online exam proctoring tool uses AI to monitor students during tests and flag prohibited behaviour such as cheating. How is this classified under the AI Act?
A political consultancy wants a generative AI chatbot that talks directly to voters and is designed to influence how they vote in a referendum. Is this high-risk under the AI Act?
A regional emergency services centre wants an AI that classifies incoming emergency calls and decides the priority of dispatching ambulances, police and fire brigades. Is it a high-risk AI system?
A border agency plans an AI system that scores travellers arriving in the Schengen area on their risk of irregular migration or security threats. How is this system classified?
What must the risk management system for a high-risk AI system consist of, and does it apply only at design time or throughout the lifecycle?
We are developing a high-risk educational AI tool used by teenagers. Do we have to consider the impact on persons under 18 in our risk management?
What documentation must a provider draw up before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, and can SMEs provide it in a simplified form?
For how long do providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems have to retain the automatically generated logs?
Does a high-risk AI system have to allow the human operator to override its output or stop it, for example with a stop button?
Our high-risk AI system keeps learning after deployment. What does the AI Act require to prevent biased outputs from feeding back into the system's future inputs?
We are a small provider of a high-risk AI system with limited staff. Can we implement our quality management system in a proportionate or simplified way?
We are an EU company importing a high-risk AI system from a non-EU vendor. What must we verify before placing it on the market?
A distributor wants to resell a high-risk AI system in the EU. What checks does it have to carry out before making the system available?
An employer plans to introduce a high-risk AI system in the workplace. Does it have to inform employees and their representatives beforehand?
A municipality is about to deploy a high-risk AI system. Which impact assessment must it carry out beforehand, and what must it contain?
Do providers of high-risk AI systems for recruitment need a notified body for the conformity assessment, or can they rely on internal control?
A public authority intends to put a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III into service. Does it have to register itself and its use of the system in the EU database?
At what moment must users be told that they are interacting with an AI system or being exposed to a deep fake, and in what form?
What criteria make a general-purpose AI model one with systemic risk, and what is the training compute threshold that creates a presumption?
What additional obligations apply to providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, such as adversarial testing and incident reporting?
If we take part in an AI regulatory sandbox and follow the sandbox plan and the authority's guidance in good faith, can we still be fined under the AI Act?
A defence contractor develops an AI system used exclusively for military purposes. Does the AI Act apply to it?
What is the legal definition of an 'AI system' in the AI Act?
A mobile app lets users upload a photo of an identifiable person and generates realistic nude images of that person without their consent. Is it legal to offer this app?
A school wants to use AI cameras to infer pupils' emotions such as boredom or frustration during lessons to adapt teaching. Is this allowed?

Our AI tool only checks whether loan application documents are complete and correctly formatted, a narrow procedural task. We believe it is not high-risk under Article 6(3). What must we do to document and register this assessment?
A company wants an AI system that predicts which employees should be promoted or dismissed based on their behaviour and performance data. How is this system classified?
A police unit wants an AI tool that assesses how reliable the evidence is in a criminal investigation. Is this a high-risk AI system?
After a burglary police want to run facial recognition on recorded CCTV footage to find suspects. What authorisation is needed for this post-remote biometric identification system?
Can we process special categories of personal data such as ethnicity to detect and correct bias in our high-risk hiring model, and under what conditions?
For a high-risk remote biometric identification system, does a deployer need to have the identification verified by more than one person before acting on it?
A bank rejected a customer's loan based on the output of its high-risk credit scoring AI. What rights does the customer have, and what must the bank tell people subject to such a system?
After a high-risk AI system has been certified, the provider makes a major change that was not foreseen in the initial assessment. Does a new conformity assessment have to be carried out?
A blog network publishes AI-generated articles on matters of public interest without any human review or editorial responsibility. Do they have to disclose that the text was artificially generated?
We release a general-purpose AI model under a free and open-source licence with public weights. Are we exempt from the documentation obligations of Article 53?
We want to test our high-risk AI system in real-world conditions outside a sandbox. What conditions must be met, and what consent do the test subjects have to give?
What are the deadlines for a provider to report a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, including cases of death or widespread infringement?
An AI system is built on a general-purpose AI model and both are developed by the same provider. Which authority is exclusively competent for supervising and enforcing the AI Act for this system?
